A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IGA research. All 28 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, proofs, and experimental appendices, are readable and support comparison across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-function, Kodak image, 3D shape, and NeRF experiments, including sampling ablations and per-image or per-scene results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds activation comparisons, resource measurements, MS-SSIM scores, and Chamfer-distance results.

M1.justification: The core grouping, sampled-eNTK construction, and inductive gradient adjustment remain unchanged. However, the stated Adam construction changes from balancing against lambda_end in v1 Section 3.3 to lambda_(end+1) in v2 Section 3.4 and Appendix D. This changes the prescribed transformation at a fixed end value; the new pseudocode otherwise explains the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic functions, first eight Kodak images, five 3D objects, and eight Blender NeRF scenes. Sampling ablations still use the first three Kodak images. Additional activations, metrics, and resource measurements do not introduce new datasets or task scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix E and Table 5 add vanilla Gauss, WIRE, and FINER comparisons against their IGA counterparts. Conversely, SIREN+BN is removed from both image and shape comparisons, with incompatibility stated in Table 1. This substantially revises architecture/comparator coverage; FR and the other BN comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds MS-SSIM for image evaluation, Chamfer distance for shapes, and per-iteration time/memory profiling across four task types. Appendix E introduces three additional activation configurations. Synthetic experiments also revise the stated end ranges from 11–15 to 10–14 and from 2–8 to 1–7; the latter accompanies the revised Adam convention. These reported changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 and Table 4 add cross-task computational-cost analysis, including a full-eNTK comparison for 1D fitting and memory limitations for larger tasks. v1 already examined sampling-group size versus runtime. Its sampling-point and group-size ablations are retained with unchanged values in v2 Tables 6–7.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten random seeds for the synthetic experiments and describe uncertainty bands as twice the standard deviation. v2 introduces no new confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting practice for the vision results.

E6.justification: v2 adds activation, MS-SSIM, Chamfer-distance, and resource results, removes SIREN+BN entries, and revises BN scores. For example, appendix PE+BN Kodak PSNR changes from 31.65 to 28.78, and ReLU+BN shape IoU from 0.9542 to 0.9662. Most original IGA scores and NeRF results remain unchanged. Reporting conflicts also appear: v2 Table 1 gives PE+FR PSNR as 31.65, whereas Table 8 retains 29.74.

T1.justification: v1 Theorems 4.1–4.2 become v2 Theorems 3.1–3.2, with informal main-text statements. Their formal assumptions, bounds, supporting lemmas, and proofs remain in Appendix A. The revisions principally change exposition and notation rather than introduce new mathematical results.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that eNTK connects training dynamics with spectral bias and that inductively generalized gradient adjustments provide scalable, controllable improvements for INRs. v2 emphasizes consistency and supplies additional evidence, but retains the central contributions and their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explicit interpretation of the accuracy/resource tradeoff, reporting average overheads of 1.56 times training time and 1.34 times memory. It also qualifies SIREN+BN applicability through an incompatibility statement and expands discussion of FR/BN instability across metrics and scenes. The main spectral-bias mechanism remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds an IGA code-access URL, Algorithm 1, detailed tensor-flattening/grouping instructions, binary voxel-label clarification, and explicit ordering of IGA before Adam updates. Existing image-training settings are relocated to Appendix G. Conversely, v1's explicit 5e-5 learning rate for synthetic Experiment 2 is omitted from v2.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on newer INR methods and surveys, including Ramasinghe and Lucey, Essakine et al., and Luo et al. It more explicitly acknowledges Geifman et al.'s use of empirical-kernel adjustment in toy settings. The overall positioning around architectural improvements versus training-dynamics adjustment remains intact.

P1.justification: The main text undergoes extensive rewriting and restructuring. Theory moves into the method section, detailed theorem statements are replaced by informal summaries, and implementation explanations are expanded. The appendices are reorganized with a roadmap and separate sampling, Adam, and activation sections; several existing experimental details move between main text and appendices.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the single-column main-text layout with two columns, adds an algorithm block and sampling diagram, and introduces resource, activation, MS-SSIM, and Chamfer-distance displays. Tables remove SIREN+BN columns or rows. Qualitative panels are reorganized, including replacing the appendix Kodak 5/6 overview with a Kodak 4 detail comparison and emphasizing Lucy close-ups.

improvement.justification: Resource profiling, tests with Gauss/WIRE/FINER, and additional perceptual/geometric metrics better support IGA's practicality and applicability. Clearer implementation explanations and code-access information also help. However, unexplained BN score revisions and new summary/appendix inconsistencies, notably PE+FR PSNR in Tables 1 and 8, weaken confidence in the revised comparisons. The evidence therefore supports a modest overall improvement.
